The family close-out card this body names, objectstack-ai/objectstack#24901, closed `completed` at 2026-10-21T02:52Z when objectstack-ai/objectstack PR #25025 merged as objectstack `main` commit **`338297e46`**. That commit changes `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` again, so a port of `7e40e8a03` alone would leave the two copies differing. This card is unclaimed, so the port is now one PR from two commits, not two PRs on the same file:

| objectstack commit | what it carries | files |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `7e40e8a03` (PR #24886) | `subst_end()` for `$(…)` and backticks, called from `strip_line_comment`, `split_segments` and `tokenize` | `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` and its self-test |
| `338297e46` (PR #25025) | `subst_end()` gains a `${…}` arm and a rule for a `'` run inside a quoted `${…}`; it now decides its own trigger, so the three call sites change shape; each copying hook carries a byte-identical copy of `subst_end()`, and its self-test pins that copy against the canonical | `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`, `guard-shared-stash.sh`, `guard-tree-enum.sh`, `guard-process-kill.sh` and their self-tests |

Measured on objectui `origin/main` `0093b2c` (2026-10-21T05:15Z): `.claude/hooks/` has `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`, `guard-shared-stash.sh` and `guard-tree-enum.sh` with their self-tests, and no `guard-process-kill.sh`; `git grep -c subst_end` there finds nothing. So the `guard-process-kill` rows of `338297e46` have no twin here and drop out of the port.

**Done when, as this memo amends it.** The body's third Done-when line (`guard-shared-stash.sh` out of scope) is superseded: `338297e46` makes the stash and tree-enum copies pinned to the main-checkout canonical, so they port in the same PR.
- `git show 7e40e8a03 338297e46 -- .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh .claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh .claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh .claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.sh .claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.selftest.sh`, in an objectstack checkout, gives the diff to port, localised as earlier ports were.
- `338297e46` also gave objectstack's `guard-tree-enum.sh` the in-quote backslash branch its siblings had. Whether objectui's copy lacks it too is NOT MEASURED here; the port measures it and carries the branch if it is missing, as the identity pin requires.
- Each ported self-test passes, its identity pin included, and every existing real-write, real-stash and tree-sweep control stays blocked.

**Do not copy one line of PR #25025's rationale.** Its body files `echo "${x:-'}'}" ; sed -i s/a/b/ pkg/x.ts` under "shapes the pre-fix reached only through the misreading itself". The contract review on that PR (objectstack-ai/objectstack#25025 comment 6306009730, ①.6) shows this is wrong: the pre-fix read that shape correctly, so allowing it is a recall regression, accepted as a declared and pinned fail-open. The hook's header and pins are right. Only that sentence of prose is wrong.

Routing and grade stay with triage.

## What this ports

A file port of two objectstack commits into the objectui copies of the Bash-guard hook family, as the card's memo 6308641120 amends its Done-when. Six files under `.claude/hooks/`:

- `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` and its self-test: objectstack `7e40e8a03` (PR 24886, the shared `subst_end()` for a `$(…)` or backtick inside a double-quoted word, called from `strip_line_comment`, `split_segments` and `tokenize`) and `338297e46` (PR 25025, a `${…}` arm and the rule for a `'` run inside a quoted `${…}`).
- `guard-shared-stash.sh` and its self-test: `338297e46` only. It carries a byte-identical `subst_end()` and delegates to it from `split_segments()`; the self-test pins that copy against the canonical.
- `guard-tree-enum.sh` and its self-test: `338297e46` only. Same copy and delegation, plus the in-quote backslash branch (an escaped quote inside a double-quoted word leaves the region open) that its two siblings already had and this copy lacked. Its self-test pins `subst_end()` against the canonical and `split_segments()` against the stash guard's.
- `guard-process-kill.sh` of `338297e46` has no twin in this repo and is not ported.

Applied as the exact objectstack diff of each file, then localised by hand where a hunk's context differed: foreign issue references carry the `objectstack#` prefix, the provenance stamp on line 2 of all six files names `338297e46018ae96256262590a308c8be735f825`, and the stash guard's header case count was re-derived (62 = 57 `expect ` lines + 2 inline specials + 2 hatch-message assertions + 1 identity pin; the self-test run prints the same total). One cleanup beyond the diff: the stash guard's `split_segments()` carried five extra comment lines inside the function body that objectstack's copy does not, which made the new byte-identity pin between the stash and tree-enum copies fail, so they are removed to match objectstack's function text.

The `subst_end()` block is byte-identical across all three hooks and equal to objectstack's copies (the same md5 for the function text, measured on all three here and on objectstack's four). The comment above it in `guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` names the two hooks here that carry the copy and says `guard-process-kill.sh` carries one in objectstack only.

Not copied: any of PR 25025's description. The card's memo says one sentence of it, about `echo "${x:-'}'}" ; sed -i s/a/b/ pkg/x.ts`, is wrong about what the pre-fix hook did. This PR copies code, headers and pins only; the declared fail-open for that shape is pinned as objectstack pins it.

## Measured

- Premise at `cd14d8e`: `subst_end` occurs 0 times in all three hooks and their self-tests; in objectstack `origin/main` (`2069b81c2`) it occurs 7 times in the main-checkout hook and 3 times each in the stash and tree-enum hooks.
- Self-tests on head `8a0c369`, via `os-verify-lock.sh`: main-checkout `157 passed, 0 failed`; shared-stash `62 passed, 0 failed`; tree-enum `50 passed, 0 failed`; all exit 0, identity pins included. Before: 130, 50 and 38 cases, all passing.
- Reverse validation, run after the commits, with the base-blob hook and the ported self-test copied to a scratch dir (tree not mutated): main-checkout `143 passed, 14 failed`; shared-stash `56 passed, 6 failed` (three false blocks, two fail-open reads, the identity pin); tree-enum `43 passed, 7 failed` (three false blocks, one fail-open read, both identity pins, plus the escaped-quote false block). All red, as predicted.
- The four commands measured on the first head now answer as objectstack's copies do (same cwd, exit codes): `echo "say \"; ls *.yml; git show origin/main:x\" ok"` through the tree-enum guard 0 (was 2); `echo "he said \"x\"" ; for f in *.yml; do git show "origin/main:$f"; done` 2 (was 0); `echo "$(printf '"')" ; git stash pop` through the stash guard 2 (was 0); `echo "$(printf '"')" ; for f in *.yml; do git show "origin/main:$f"; done` through the tree-enum guard 2 (was 0). The card's two curl forms exit 0 and `echo hi > out.txt` exits 2 through the main-checkout guard.
- Every pre-existing real-write, real-stash and tree-sweep case still passes unchanged.

## Remaining differences from objectstack (none is hook logic)

Compared against objectstack `338297e46` with comment lines removed: the main-checkout hook differs only in the worktree-recipe help text's issue reference and the selftest's example strings. The tree-enum hook differs in one help-text word and example strings. The stash guard differs more, in text that comes from other objectstack changes, not these two commits: its printed help message (a shorter list of alternatives) and a handful of self-test cases (objectstack has extra `echo \" ; git stash ...` cases that this repo's matrix words differently). Left as they are; the escaped-quote logic itself is present and pinned here.
